prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has concussion. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1067; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Can you please state your full name for the record?

A: I'd rather not give my name on the recording, if that's okay. You already have it on the claim.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was driving on the main road in Pasadena, Texas, heading toward the shopping center. Traffic had slowed down ahead of me, so I was stopped at a light.

Q: Did you have any warning before the impact?

A: Not really. I looked in my mirror and saw the car coming, but there wasn't time to move. It hit me from behind pretty hard.

Q: Were you wearing a seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was. The airbag didn't deploy, but my head snapped forward and then back against the headrest.

Q: How are you feeling now?

A: Not great. I've had headaches almost every day since it happened. Bright lights bother my eyes, and I get dizzy if I stand up too fast. My doctor said I have a concussion.

Q: Have you seen a doctor since the accident?

A: Yes, I went to the emergency room the same day, and I've been following up with my primary care physician. I've also been referred to a specialist, and I have another appointment next week.

Q: Are you having any trouble working or with daily tasks?

A: I've had to take time off. Concentrating on screens for long periods gives me a headache, so I've been doing shorter shifts when I can.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I want to make sure my medical bills and lost time are documented properly. Thank you for your patience.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
